hints: Plot cumulative frequencies at the upper class boundaries: $(20, 12)$, $(30, 48)$, $(40, 106)$, $(60, 134)$, and $(100, 150)$.
Anchor the lower end of the curve at $(0, 0)$ since the minimum time is 0.
Use linear scales on both axes: horizontal axis from 0 to 100 minutes, vertical axis from 0 to 150 students.
Join the plotted points with a smooth curve or connected line segments and label axes.
walkthrough:
Identify the points $(t, \text{cumulative frequency})$ to plot at the upper boundaries:
$$(0, 0), \; (20, 12), \; (30, 48), \; (40, 106), \; (60, 134), \; (100, 150)$$

Draw linear scales on both axes:
$$\text{Horizontal axis}: \text{Time taken, } t \text{ (minutes)}, \text{ from } 0 \text{ to } 100$$
$$\text{Vertical axis}: \text{Cumulative frequency, from } 0 \text{ to } 150$$
Plot each point accurately and join them with a smooth cumulative frequency curve starting from $(0, 0)$.
teacher_walkthrough:
We are given a cumulative frequency table for 150 students completing a challenge:
- $t \le 20$: 12
- $t \le 30$: 48
- $t \le 40$: 106
- $t \le 60$: 134
- $t \le 100$: 150

Step 1: Identify coordinates to plot.
In a cumulative frequency graph, cumulative frequency is always plotted at the upper boundary of each class:
$$(20, 12), \; (30, 48), \; (40, 106), \; (60, 134), \; (100, 150)$$
The lower anchor point is $(0, 0)$ because no student completes the challenge in 0 minutes or less.

Step 2: Choose suitable scales.
- Horizontal axis: Time $t$ (minutes) spanning 0 to 100 (e.g. 2 cm per 20 minutes).
- Vertical axis: Cumulative frequency spanning 0 to 150 (e.g. 2 cm per 20 or 25 students).

Step 3: Plot and connect.
Plot all six points accurately and connect them with an increasing smooth S-shaped curve (an ogive). Label the horizontal axis 'Time (minutes)' and the vertical axis 'Cumulative frequency'.

hints: If 24% of students take $k$ minutes or longer, then $100\% - 24\% = 76\%$ take less than $k$ minutes.
Locate 114 on the vertical cumulative frequency axis and read across to the curve.
Read down to the horizontal axis to find $k \approx 45$ minutes.
walkthrough:
Determine the cumulative frequency corresponding to the 76th percentile (the lower $76\%$ who take less than $k$ minutes):
$$\text{Rank} = 150 \times (1 - 0.24) = 150 \times 0.76 = 114$$

Read from the cumulative frequency graph at vertical value 114 across to the curve and down to the horizontal time axis:
$$k \approx 45\text{ minutes}$$
teacher_walkthrough: We are told that 24% of the 150 students take $k$ minutes or longer to complete the challenge, and we need to estimate $k$ from our graph.

Step 1: Translate the upper-tail percentage into cumulative frequency.
Since cumulative frequency measures the number of students taking less than or equal to a given time:
$$\text{Percentage taking less than } k = 100\% - 24\% = 76\%$$

Step 2: Find the corresponding student count:
$$\text{Cumulative frequency} = 150 \times 0.76 = 114$$

Step 3: Read from the graph.
Locate $114$ on the vertical cumulative frequency axis.
Draw a horizontal line across to meet the cumulative frequency curve.
From that point on the curve, draw a vertical line down to meet the horizontal axis.
The value on the time axis is approximately $45$ minutes.
Thus, $k \approx 45$ minutes.

hints: Extract class intervals and frequencies by taking successive differences of the cumulative frequencies: $12, 36, 58, 28, 16$.
Find the midpoint $t$ for each class interval: $10, 25, 35, 50, 80$.
Calculate the estimated mean: $\bar{t} = \dfrac{\sum f t}{\sum f} = \dfrac{120 + 900 + 2030 + 1400 + 1280}{150} = \dfrac{5730}{150}$.
Calculate estimated variance: $\dfrac{\sum f t^2}{\sum f} - \bar{t}^2 = \dfrac{267\,150}{150} - (38.2)^2$, then take the square root to find the standard deviation.
walkthrough:
Calculate the estimated mean:
$$\bar{t} = \dfrac{\sum f t}{\sum f} = \dfrac{5\,730}{150} = 38.2\text{ minutes}$$

Calculate the estimated variance and standard deviation:
$$\text{Variance} = \dfrac{\sum f t^2}{\sum f} - \bar{t}^2 = \dfrac{267\,150}{150} - (38.2)^2 = 1\,781 - 1\,459.24 = 321.76$$
$$\text{Standard deviation} = \sqrt{321.76} \approx 17.938 \approx 17.9\text{ minutes}$$
teacher_walkthrough: We need to calculate estimates of the mean and standard deviation of the challenge completion times from the cumulative frequency table.

Step 1: Deduce group frequencies from the cumulative frequency table:
- Class $0 < t \le 20$: frequency $= 12$
- Class $20 < t \le 30$: frequency $= 48 - 12 = 36$
- Class $30 < t \le 40$: frequency $= 106 - 48 = 58$
- Class $40 < t \le 60$: frequency $= 134 - 106 = 28$
- Class $60 < t \le 100$: frequency $= 150 - 134 = 16$
Total frequency $\sum f = 12 + 36 + 58 + 28 + 16 = 150$.

Step 2: Find the midpoints ($t$) of each class:
- Midpoint of $(0, 20)$: $\frac{0 + 20}{2} = 10$
- Midpoint of $(20, 30)$: $\frac{20 + 30}{2} = 25$
- Midpoint of $(30, 40)$: $\frac{30 + 40}{2} = 35$
- Midpoint of $(40, 60)$: $\frac{40 + 60}{2} = 50$
- Midpoint of $(60, 100)$: $\frac{60 + 100}{2} = 80$

Step 3: Calculate $\sum f t$:
$$\sum f t = (12 \times 10) + (36 \times 25) + (58 \times 35) + (28 \times 50) + (16 \times 80)$$
$$\sum f t = 120 + 900 + 2030 + 1400 + 1280 = 5730$$
$$\text{Estimated mean } \bar{t} = \frac{5730}{150} = 38.2 \text{ minutes}$$

Step 5: Compute variance and standard deviation:
$$\operatorname{Var}(T) = \frac{\sum f t^2}{\sum f} - \bar{t}^2 = \frac{267150}{150} - (38.2)^2$$
$$\operatorname{Var}(T) = 1781 - 1459.24 = 321.76$$
$$\sigma = \sqrt{321.76} \approx 17.93766... \approx 17.9 \text{ minutes}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives mean $= 38.2$ minutes and standard deviation $= 17.9$ minutes.
